notes:
CIRCUIT: a three-branch parallel network hung between a top rail and a grounded bottom rail, with a mid-height rail that is broken by two DC voltage sources. Top rail y~262-290 runs from (206,262) to (781,290). Three vertical columns drop from it: left x~210 (10R#0, then 4H#6), middle x~515-545 (20R#2, then 1F#7, then on to GND#8), right x~765-781 (30R#1, then I-DC#5 '2A'). Mid rail y~488-497 runs from the left column at (219,488) through V-DC#3 '60V' (leads at x=328 and x=446), across the middle column at (521,489), through V-DC#4 (leads at x=575 and x=679), to the right column at (775,494). Bottom rail y~723-731 runs from the left column corner (232,723) to the right column corner (781,731); GND#8 hangs below it on the middle column.

NET MAP (5 nets, 9 components):
  n1 = top rail: 10R#0 top, 20R#2 top, 30R#1 top.
  n2 = left column between 10R#0 bottom and 4H#6 top, plus the mid-rail stub out to the left lead of the 60V source: 10R#0 bottom, V-DC#3 left, 4H#6 top.
  n4 = middle column between 20R#2 bottom and 1F#7 top, plus the mid-rail segment between the two sources: 20R#2 bottom, V-DC#3 right, V-DC#4 left, 1F#7 top.
  n3 = right column between 30R#1 bottom and I-DC#5 top, plus the mid-rail stub from the right lead of V-DC#4: 30R#1 bottom, V-DC#4 right, I-DC#5 top.
  0  = bottom rail + GND#8: 4H#6 bottom, 1F#7 bottom, I-DC#5 bottom, GND#8.
So the circuit is: three resistors fan out from node n1 to n2/n4/n3; each of those three nodes has one element to ground (4H, 1F, 2A source); and the two 60V-class DC sources bridge n2-n4 and n4-n3 along the mid rail. Textbook nodal-analysis exercise, and every net has 3 or 4 terminals.

JUDGEMENT CALL 1 - S6 (517,488) + S7 (525,490), the middle column crossing the mid rail. CALLED JUNCTION (the tracer default; these are two degree-3 nodes the skeletoniser made out of one crossing).
  Ink at 10x: the descending column is drawn in two overlapping pen strokes, x=512-515 for y=455-472 and x=517-521 for y=463-487, meeting in a small check-mark kink at y=469-471; below the rail it continues at x=522-526. So the line drifts right monotonically (513 -> 519 -> 524) - there is no return step, i.e. it is NOT the sideways-jog no-connect idiom, and there is no semicircular hop and no solder dot (dot_score 1.6, the lowest on the sheet). It is a plain X.
  Why junction: this sheet contains no hops anywhere, so a plain X is the drafter's only crossing form and the dataset prior applies. More decisively, the alternative gives a node consisting of nothing but V-DC#3's right terminal and V-DC#4's left terminal - two ideal voltage sources in series with nothing at their midpoint, which is a degenerate node no netlist would specify - and it would strand 20R#2 + 1F#7 as a private series RC from the top rail to ground. The junction reading instead produces the symmetric 3-branch network described above, in which all three columns tie into the mid rail. Consequence of the other reading: 6 nets instead of 5; n4 splits into {20R bottom, 1F top} and {V-DC#3 right, V-DC#4 left}.

JUDGEMENT CALL 2 - S10 (545,730), the middle column crossing the bottom rail on its way down to GND#8. CALLED JUNCTION (tracer default, dot_score 2.6).
  Ink: the 3-4 px column swells into a solid wedge of ink roughly x=538-548, y=712-733 exactly where it meets the rail, then leaves at normal width below and runs to the GND lead at (544,759). That swelling is a drawn junction dot; there is no hop and no jog.
  Circuit sense agrees: read as a crossing, net '0' would be only {1F#7 bottom, GND#8} while the bottom rail {4H#6 bottom, I-DC#5 bottom} became a separate node - the capacitor branch would then have no return path to the rest of the circuit (its bottom would touch nothing but the ground symbol), which is not a sensible circuit. As a junction the bottom rail is simply the ground rail, which is what the drawing plainly looks like. Consequence of the other reading: 6 nets, and a dead capacitor branch.

OTHER SITES: S1 (523,282) middle column T's onto the top rail - junction, left as default. S5 (219,488) mid rail's left end T's onto the left column - junction. S8 (775,494) mid rail's right end T's onto the right column - junction. All three are wire-ends-on-wire and cannot be read any other way. S0 (206,273) is the top-left corner, where the left column overshoots the top rail by ~10 px, and S3 (548,362) is the '20R' label touching the resistor; both are non-critical and were left alone.

PORTS/CLASSES: no port overrides were needed - every '->tN' lead in the component montage is a real wire end. The three stray port candidates the tracer flagged are label ink: #1 p1 (801,355) is the '3' of '30R', #2 p2 (545,363) is the '2' of '20R', #5 p2 (839,604) is the '2' of '2A'. All nine classes match the drawing: 10R/20R/30R zigzag resistors, two circle-with-plus-minus V-DC (the '60V' at 388,486 and the unlabelled one at 627,494), a circle-with-up-arrow I-DC '2A', a 4H coil inductor, a 1F parallel-plate capacitor and one GND. No 3-terminal parts, so no pin-order questions. 3 gap bridges found, none affect the netlist, none dropped. No component is left unconnected.

NOTE ON THE SITE KEYS: S1/S5/S6/S7/S8/S10 are written out explicitly as 'junction' even though that is also the tracer default, so that this file records a deliberate decision for every critical site rather than an absence of one.
